channel.title: Teach Me One Thing
channel.description: A five-minute lesson on one interesting thing, every weekday morning.
channel.itunes:author: Aaryan
channel.itunes:summary: A five-minute lesson on one interesting thing, every weekday morning.

item.title: Why a haircut keeps getting expensive
item.description: Services like teaching, nursing and live music get costlier every decade not because they got worse, but because everyone else got more productive.

item.title: Why glass is transparent
item.description: Glass lets light through not because it has gaps, but because its electrons cannot absorb the energy visible light carries.

item.title: The invention is in the corners
item.description: Shipping got cheap not because ships got faster but because a standardized steel box cut the cost of touching cargo by ninety seven percent.

item.title: Why the sun is a terrible furnace
item.description: The core of the sun makes less heat per cubic meter than your own body, and that feebleness is exactly why life had time to happen.

item.title: Why ice is slippery
item.description: The pressure melting story you were taught is wrong; ice is slippery because its top few molecular layers are already liquid before you touch them.

item.title: The metal that was worth more than gold
item.description: Aluminum is the most common metal in the crust, but it stayed invisible for all of human history because its grip on oxygen could only be broken by electricity.

item.title: Half of you was made in a factory
item.description: About half the nitrogen atoms in your body came out of an industrial reactor, because life cannot break the bond that locks nitrogen in the air.

item.title: How a tree beats the best pump on Earth
item.description: Suction cannot lift water past ten meters, yet a redwood raises it a hundred, using stretched water under negative pressure pulled by evaporating leaves.

item.title: The machine that seems to break physics
item.description: A heat pump gives out three or four times the energy it uses because it moves heat instead of making it, and your refrigerator is the same machine pointed the other way.

item.title: Why a bicycle stays up
item.description: The gyroscope explanation for bicycle stability is wrong, and the real answer is one condition that several different mechanisms can satisfy.

item.title: Why the microwave doesn't heat by resonance
item.description: A microwave doesn't resonate water molecules; it twists them billions of times a second and the internal friction is the heat.

item.title: Why honey never spoils
item.description: Honey outlasts empires because it is a sealed desert too dry, too acidic, and too antiseptic for microbes to survive.

item.title: Why your GPS needs Einstein
item.description: GPS satellite clocks are built deliberately wrong so relativity makes them right.
